_readme: Peer-plane target verdict corpus (issue #842 W2.1).
The peer path confinement is implemented three times: `peer_target_allowed`
in packages/tunnel/data-plane/src/iroh_relay.rs (the production relay),
`isPeerPlaneTarget` in packages/tunnel/src/protocol.ts (the pure-JS
endpoint), and the route-layer re-check in
packages/server/src/routes/peer-plane.ts. A divergence between them is a
privilege question, not a style question, and it fails nowhere but on a
real link.
This file is the shared verdict corpus: each vector states the ONE answer
every implementation must give for `target`. It is read by
packages/tunnel/src/peer-target-differential.test.ts, which also drives a
seeded fast-check generator whose nastiest finds are curated back here.
`pins` is empty and the schema keeps it. It once carried
`bare-prefix-admitted-by-query-or-fragment`, the class where both guards
applied their 'must extend the prefix' test to the whole target instead of
to the path; #846 P6 fixed both languages, so those four vectors now record
`false` and stay here as the regression lock. A vector may still be pinned
in future (docs/decisions.md, ruling A-pinned) — it must name an id
explained below.
Every `target` here is representable as a Rust `&str` (well-formed UTF-8,
no lone surrogates) so the corpus can be read by a Rust test unchanged.

vectors.name: linkRedeem
vectors.note: Real peer route.

vectors.name: linkHello
vectors.note: Real peer route.

vectors.name: routeAssert
vectors.note: Real peer route.

vectors.name: blobWithQuery
vectors.note: Query is not part of the confined path.

vectors.name: fragment
vectors.note: Fragment is not part of the confined path.

vectors.name: queryCarriesTraversal
vectors.note: Dot segments in the QUERY climb nothing: the path is what is concatenated onto the upstream URL.

vectors.name: emptySegment
vectors.note: An empty segment is neither '.' nor '..' and resolves inside the plane.

vectors.name: pathParameterTraversal
vectors.note: Adversarial: '..;' is the Tomcat-style path-parameter traversal. Safe HERE only because nothing downstream strips ';' — the segment is literal.

vectors.name: fullwidthDotConfusable
vectors.note: Adversarial: U+FF0E FULLWIDTH FULL STOP. Safe only because no implementation NFKC-normalises the target; the segment stays literal.

vectors.name: authorityLookingSegment
vectors.note: Adversarial: userinfo + port. A path segment cannot become an authority once the target is proved to start with the absolute prefix.

vectors.name: gatewayNamedSegment
vectors.note: A segment SPELLED like the owner surface is still inside the plane.

vectors.name: nonAsciiSegment
vectors.note: Multi-byte UTF-8: no forbidden byte, and the byte-length test and the UTF-16 length test agree because the prefix is ASCII.

vectors.name: astralSegment
vectors.note: Astral plane (surrogate PAIR, well-formed). Rust byte length 20, JS UTF-16 length 18 — both exceed the prefix.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.note: Boundary: empty target.

vectors.name: root
vectors.note: Boundary: shorter than the prefix.

vectors.name: prefixMinusSlash
vectors.note: Boundary: one byte short of the prefix.

vectors.name: barePrefix
vectors.note: Boundary: the prefix names no resource.

vectors.name: prefixSiblingName
vectors.note: A longer name that merely starts the same way.

vectors.name: doubleLeadingSlash
vectors.note: Authority trick: '//host' would reparse as a network-path reference.

vectors.name: upperCasePrefix
vectors.note: Case game: the prefix match is case-sensitive in both languages.

vectors.name: mixedCasePrefix
vectors.note: Case game, single letter.

vectors.name: absoluteUrl
vectors.note: Authority trick: a full URL never starts with the absolute prefix.

vectors.name: leadingSpace
vectors.note: Whitespace game: no implementation trims.

vectors.name: ownerSurface
vectors.note: The escalation this guard exists to refuse.

vectors.name: vaultSurface
vectors.note: Outside the plane.

vectors.name: dotDotSegment
vectors.note: Literal traversal.

vectors.name: dotThenDotDot
vectors.note: Mixed dot segments.

vectors.name: deepTraversal
vectors.note: Traversal after a legitimate segment.

vectors.name: trailingDotDot
vectors.note: Boundary: traversal as the only extension.

vectors.name: trailingDot
vectors.note: Boundary: current-directory segment.

vectors.name: percentEncodedDotDot
vectors.note: Single escape: refused by the blanket '%' rule, not by decoding.

vectors.name: percentEncodedUpperCase
vectors.note: Case game inside the escape.

vectors.name: percentEncodedSlash
vectors.note: Encoded separator.

vectors.name: doublePercentEncoded
vectors.note: Double escape: a decode-once implementation would be fooled; the blanket rule is not.

vectors.name: overlongUtf8Escape
vectors.note: Overlong UTF-8 encoding of '/'.

vectors.name: overlongUtf8EscapeThreeByte
vectors.note: Three-byte overlong encoding of '/'.

vectors.name: loneTrailingPercent
vectors.note: Malformed escape.

vectors.name: backslashTraversal
vectors.note: Windows separator.

vectors.name: backslashPrefixed
vectors.note: Backslash after a literal '..' fragment.

vectors.name: space
vectors.note: 0x20 is refused: request-line splitting.

vectors.name: nullByte
vectors.note: NUL truncation game.

vectors.name: tab
vectors.note: Control byte.

vectors.name: unitSeparator
vectors.note: Boundary: 0x1f is the last refused control byte.

vectors.name: crlfInjection
vectors.note: Request smuggling attempt.

vectors.name: barePrefixWithQuery
vectors.note: REGRESSION LOCK (#846 P6). The path behind this target is the bare prefix, which names no peer-plane route; every implementation refuses it. Was pinned as `bare-prefix-admitted-by-query-or-fragment` until the extension test moved from the whole target onto the path.
